title: Mara and the Vector
premise: Lena Nakamura has spent eleven years as the sole caretaker of Verdance Station, a terraforming greenhouse orbiting a dead world, tending seed banks for colonists who may never come and maintaining a beacon whose original purpose was quietly erased from all records. When the warship Perihelion returns from a deep-space interdiction with its crew biologically aged backward into children and adolescents — victims of an experimental temporal weapon gone wrong — Lena's beacon is revealed to be the only receiver capable of decoding the ship's corrupted black-box message: proof that the enemy fleet never fired first. With the armistice expiring in nineteen days and both fleets converging on Verdance, Lena must choose between remaining invisible and broadcasting a truth that will end the war but expose her own buried identity as the daughter of the admiral who ordered the cover-up. She broadcasts the message; the truth stops the fleets, but at the cost of the station's destruction, and Lena finally claims her name, her inheritance, and a place among the children she helps carry home.
about_author: C. M. Oyelaran is a former agricultural systems engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. Their work explores the quiet violence of institutions and the people who keep things alive inside them.

chapters.title: The Garden Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A day in the routine of Verdance Station: pruning, nutrient cycles, logging the beacon's heartbeat pulse. She talks to the seedlings about the people they're meant for. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Beacon 7-Null
chapters.summary: Lena investigates why the beacon's maintenance records terminate eleven years ago, mid-entry, signed by someone named Nakamura. Her own surname. Emotional beat: first hairline crack in her carefully sealed past.

chapters.title: Contact Light
chapters.summary: The station's long-range array catches a deceleration burn no schedule predicts. Lena watches a warship — the Perihelion — crawl toward her garden. POV shifts briefly to the ship's failing logs. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: Children of the Perihelion
chapters.summary: The Perihelion docks under automatics. Its crew are children in adult-sized uniforms, memories fragmented, bodies aged backward by decades. The eldest, a girl called Vess, remembers only 'the light came early.' Emotional beat: horror and protectiveness colliding.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Lena decrypts a fragment of the black box: a countdown to armistice expiry and a partial phrase — 'first strike originated.' Both fleets will converge here when the truce lapses. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only adult in the room.

chapters.title: Rations and Bedtime
chapters.summary: Domestic chapter: forty-one children aboard a greenhouse station. Lena improvises schools, bunks among the hydroponics racks. Vess tests her authority. Emotional beat: reluctant family forming.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Vess recognizes the beacon's pulse pattern from shipboard training — it's a fleet-grade decryption key, decommissioned officially but still live. Someone wanted it hidden, not destroyed. Emotional beat: Lena realizes she was left here deliberately.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Daughter
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lena's POV. Eleven years ago: her father, Admiral Nakamura, falsified the first-strike record to preserve the truce, then hid his whistleblower daughter where no one would look — tending his secret insurance policy. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with love.

chapters.title: Scavengers
chapters.summary: A salvage tug arrives asking questions about the Perihelion's distress ping. Lena plays the invisible caretaker while Vess hides the children. The tug leaves — but transmits their coordinates. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: The Message, Fragmented
chapters.summary: Working with Vess's half-memories, Lena reconstructs more of the black box: sensor data proving the enemy fleet's weapons were cold when the 'attack' occurred. But three key packets are corrupted beyond the station's tools. Emotional beat: hope with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Little Fleet
chapters.summary: The children, many retaining muscle memory of naval drill, begin restoring the Perihelion's shuttle bay under Vess's command. Lena resists militarizing her garden; Vess argues survival requires it. Emotional beat: ideological friction between protection and preparation.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: A sabotage attempt freezes two growing bays. Someone reached the station — or something already aboard did. Suspicion falls on a child who doesn't remember the last six hours. Emotional beat: trust fracturing in the small community.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was a Weapons Officer
chapters.summary: POV chapter for Tam, age nine, body of a nine-year-old, mind carrying reflexes for targeting systems he can't consciously access. He fears what he might do. Lena promises him he is not his training. Emotional beat: compassion as resistance to fate.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena uses the beacon to query archived fleet traffic and finds her father's last transmission, addressed to her, sealed. It requires a decryption key she doesn't have — yet its header matches the corrupted black-box packets. Emotional beat: grief pulling her toward the truth.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Both fleets alter course toward Verdance. The salvage tug's transmission worked. Nineteen days becomes twelve. Vess urges broadcasting everything now; Lena insists a partial truth could ignite the war instead of ending it. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of timing.

chapters.title: Greenhouse Siege
chapters.summary: An advance scout drone breaches the hull. The children execute a flawless defensive drill — too flawless, coordinated like veterans. Lena watches her garden become a garrison. Emotional beat: mourning the innocence she can't preserve.

chapters.title: Vess Remembers
chapters.summary: Under the beacon's resonance field, Vess recovers a memory: the Perihelion's captain ordered the temporal weapon fired preemptively, on falsified orders — orders traced back to Admiral Nakamura's chain of command. Emotional beat: Vess's hero-worship of Lena curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Vess accuses Lena of being part of the cover-up. Lena admits her name but not her father's plan. The children overhear. Trust collapses. Emotional beat: the cost of inherited secrets.

chapters.title: Exile in the Bays
chapters.summary: The children lock Lena out of command spaces and run the station themselves, competently, coldly. Alone among her plants, Lena confronts whether she ever belonged anywhere. Emotional beat: exile as mirror.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam, torn between both mother figures, secretly restores Lena's access — using his feared weapons-officer instincts to override locks without harming anyone. He asks her to teach him who he could be instead. Emotional beat: chosen loyalty over assigned identity.

chapters.title: The Sealed Transmission
chapters.summary: With Tam's help, Lena opens her father's final message: he confesses everything, including that the beacon holds the complete uncorrupted black-box copy — the corruption was inserted remotely, after arrival, by someone still listening. Emotional beat: posthumous absolution and new terror.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: They trace the remote corruption signal to the salvage tug, still shadowing the station. Aboard: an intelligence officer aged backward like the crew — the saboteur-child from Chapter 12, a planted asset. Emotional beat: the war reaching into the nursery.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Fleets now visible as moving stars. The saboteur-child offers a trade: the true black box for the children's return to fleet custody. Vess wants to accept; Lena refuses to hand them back to the institution that broke them. Emotional beat: justice versus safety.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small
chapters.summary: The children vote. Not for Lena's plan or Vess's — for their own: they will deliver the message themselves, flying the restored shuttles, refusing to be cargo in anyone's peace. Emotional beat: agency seized.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End
chapters.summary: Training montage chapter: shuttles, relay chains, the beacon's broadcast sequence rehearsed across the station's arrays. Lena teaches, learns, apologizes. Reconciliation with Vess, incomplete but real. Emotional beat: repair.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Story
chapters.summary: Lena speaks privately with the intelligence officer-child, who remembers being an adult spy and hates it. They don't surrender the officer, but learn the enemy fleet believes Verdance is a weapons platform. Emotional beat: enemy revealed as another damaged child of the war.

chapters.title: Broadcast Eve
chapters.summary: Final preparations. Lena writes her own log entry to replace the one terminated eleven years ago, signing her full name. She seeds the vault with a backup of everything. Emotional beat: quiet courage before the storm.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: The vanguard of both fleets arrives simultaneously. Hails demand surrender of 'the Perihelion assets.' Lena opens a channel and speaks as the beacon's keeper — the voice nobody remembered commissioning. Emotional beat: invisibility ended on her terms.

chapters.title: Nineteen Hours
chapters.summary: Negotiation under guns. Each fleet accuses the other; the truce clock bleeds down. Lena stalls, buying hours for the children's shuttle relay to reach optimal broadcast geometry. Emotional beat: tension stretched to filament.

chapters.title: The Shot
chapters.summary: A trigger-happy destroyer fires on the Perihelion's hulk. No deaths — but the fleets go to alert. The children launch early, scattered, exposed. Emotional beat: catastrophe tipping off the edge.

chapters.title: Relay
chapters.summary: POV rotates through the shuttle pilots — Vess, Tam, others — threading between two armadas, handing the broadcast packet beacon to beacon. One shuttle takes damage; Tam's targeting instincts save it without firing a shot. Emotional beat: competence as redemption.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Said
chapters.summary: The full black-box message goes out on every channel: sensor truths, the captain's confession, Admiral Nakamura's sealed testimony. Both fleets receive it in the open, undeniable. Emotional beat: silence across two armadas.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at Verdance
chapters.summary: Weapons stand down in staggered, disbelieving increments. Commanders demand verification; the raw data withstands it. The war doesn't end with signatures — it ends with everyone having heard the same truth at once. Emotional beat: exhale after nineteen days.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Broadcast feedback and the earlier destroyer strike cascade: Verdance Station's core fails. Evacuation to the fleet ships — the children leaving the only home some of them remember. Lena stays to shepherd the last seed vault pods out. Emotional beat: grief for a place that made her.

chapters.title: Last Light in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Alone in the failing station, Lena walks her garden one final time, planting nothing, thanking everything. She launches the seed pods toward the terraformed world below — the garden delivered at last. Emotional beat: elegy turned benediction.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Aboard the flagship, Lena faces an inquiry — and declines to let her father's name be either damned or sanctified. She testifies as herself. The tribunal acknowledges the beacon's commissioning: her father's final act was leaving her the choice. Emotional beat: claiming authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: The Children's Fleet
chapters.summary: The aged-backward crew, unable to return to their old lives, petition to form a new service — witnesses, archivists, keepers of the record so falsification can't happen again. Vess leads; Tam enlists as an educator. Emotional beat: belonging built rather than granted.

chapters.title: Groundfall
chapters.summary: The seed pods reach the surface; the first green breaks soil on the dead world, years ahead of schedule because the war's end freed the terraforming fleet. Lena descends to see it. Emotional beat: the future arriving early, gently.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: On the new world, the children give Lena a name from their fragmented ship-culture: Mara, 'the one who keeps.' She accepts it alongside Nakamura, holding both. Emotional beat: wholeness — inheritance and chosen family reconciled.

chapters.title: The Beacon Still Sings
chapters.summary: Epilogue, five years later. A rebuilt beacon on the young world pulses its message of verified record across the dark. Lena tends a garden for people already born, teaching them to listen. Final line echoes Chapter 1's ritual, transformed. Emotional beat: peace as ongoing practice.
